quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 headline results (CEO Dara Khosrowshahi): top line and profitability at or above the high end of guidance; gross bookings up 21% year on year, trip and audience-led with audience growing 17%; Mobility gross bookings accelerated to 20% with record margins; Delivery grew 23%; Freight returned to growth; non-GAAP EPS increased 44% year-over-year; a record $3 billion returned to shareholders through buybacks
quarterly_data.figure: Gross bookings were up 21%; Mobility gross bookings accelerated to 20%; Delivery grew 23%; Non-GAAP EPS increased 44%; record $3 billion buybacks

quarterly_data.signal: AV scale-up status: more than 30 autonomous partners across mobility and delivery, deployments scaling globally; AV mobility trips grew more than 10x year-on-year; on track to be live in up to 15 cities by the end of the year including new U.S. deployments, and 'significantly more than that going into next year'; launched Uber Autonomous Solutions to provide technical and operational infrastructure (fleet management, data collection) so AV partners can focus on building the driver and commercialize faster
quarterly_data.figure: more than 30 autonomous partners; AV mobility trips grew more than 10x year-on-year; up to 15 cities by the end of the year

quarterly_data.signal: AV market view and competitive read: CEO calls AVs 'another trillion-dollar TAM' and not a winner-take-all market; sees no effect of Waymo launches on Uber's overall business, performance with Waymo in Austin and Atlanta continues to be strong, and Uber's category position in San Francisco and L.A. is higher than six months ago; CFO says incremental AV adoption in SF and L.A. has been expansionary for ridesharing in aggregate

AV bottleneck: asked about scaling constraints, the CEO said 'Right now I'd say the blockers are we just need more cars on the road'; vehicles are introduced with a safety driver removed once partners pass Uber's safety case (e.g. Abu Dhabi and Dubai); regulator dialogue on AV behavior (power outages, school zones, first responders) will take time; partnerships range from Zoox and Nuro/Lucid to Pony, WeRide and Baidu in the international markets

Building the AV fleet ecosystem so AVs can scale to hundreds of millions of trips: fleet management (new relationship with Hertz), securing depots in regulation-ready markets, charging/repair/cleaning, a financing deal with Santander (AV residual values not yet clear, but AVs on Uber's network have predictable trips per vehicle per day at a premium to 1P networks, enabling a capital-light financing ecosystem), and insurance with Marsh and Apollo (management expects AV insurance to be cheaper than human insurance)

AI spending: CFO said that when Uber set its 2026 budgets in November it underestimated the impact AI tools could have, and it has re-upped that investment, trading it off against incremental headcount growth; CEO said Uber's investment in AI tools and infrastructure is increasing, offset by slower headcount growth, and that about 10% of code is now committed by autonomous agents
quarterly_data.figure: About 10% of our codes now is committed
